Manifold Bio is a platform biotechnology company pioneering AI-guided protein design and massively multiplexed in vivo screening to unlock tissue-targeted medicines and organism-scale models of living systems. Using proprietary molecular barcoding technology, we screen hundreds of thousands of protein designs simultaneously in living systems, producing in vivo-validated datasets at a scale no one else can match. The datasets power our computational models, which leads to better drug designs, creating a flywheel that gets stronger with every campaign. Our team of protein engineers, biologists, and computational scientists works across this full stack to pursue programs both internally and with leading pharma companies.
PositionManifold Bio is seeking a talented Machine Learning Research Engineer to join our growing AI team. You will work closely with our research scientists to implement, scale, and optimize machine learning systems that power our de novo antibody design platform and advance our protein design capabilities. Your efforts will contribute to building production-ready ML infrastructure that enables breakthrough discoveries in protein therapeutics. You will be expected to take ownership of engineering challenges in our ML pipeline, from data processing and model training to deployment and monitoring, while collaborating closely with our research team to translate cutting-edge ideas into robust, scalable systems.This is an on-site role and can be based in either Boston, Massachusetts or San Francisco, California. Please only apply if you reside in these cities or are open to relocate. 
ResponsibilitiesImplement and optimize machine learning models for protein designBuild and maintain scalable data processing pipelines for large-scale protein and molecular datasetsDevelop and deploy ML infrastructure for distributed training and inference across GPU clustersCollaborate with research scientists to translate experimental ML approaches into production-ready codeDesign and execute ML experiments with clear hypotheses and rigorous analysisOptimize model performance and computational efficiency for large-scale protein design tasksBuild tools and utilities to support rapid prototyping and experimentation by the research team
Required QualificationsBachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computational Biology, or related field2+ years of hands-on experience with PyTorch and/or JAX for deep learning applicationsStrong proficiency in Python scientific computing stack (NumPy, Pandas, scikit-learn)Experience with distributed computing and GPU optimization techniquesFamiliarity with protein structure analysis, computational biology, or analogous problems in natural sciencesUnderstanding of modern deep learning architectures and optimization techniquesExperience implementing research papers or translating ML approaches to production systemsProficiency with version control (Git), testing frameworks, and software engineering best practicesStrong problem-solving skills and ability to work independently on technical challengesExcellent written and verbal communication skills for cross-functional collaborationPreferred QualificationsExperience training LLMs or diffusion generative modelsKnowledge of cloud computing platforms (AWS, GCP) and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes)Background in computational biology, bioinformatics, or structural biologyExperience with large-scale data engineering and ETL pipelinesFamiliarity with MLOps practices and model deployment frameworksThis Role Might Be Perfect For You IfYou are passionate about leveraging state of the art machine learning approaches to solve challenging disease areasYou enjoy translating research ideas into high impact, productionized, scalable codeYou have rich AI/ML experience and are looking to pivot into biotechIf you're excited to build scalable ML systems that revolutionize protein therapeutic discovery, please reach out to careers@manifold.bio.Base Salary Range: $140,000-225,000This reflects the typical offer range for this role, based on experience, role scope, and internal equity. Final compensation decisions are made using a consistent leveling framework and consider the candidate’s experience, interview performance, and expected impact.This Role Is Eligible ForAnnual performance-based target bonusStock optionsComprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage401(k) planFlexible paid time off and holidaysPerks including on-site gym, onsite lunch, and commuter supportOur compensation ranges are reviewed annually to ensure alignment with market trends and internal equity.We value different experiences and ways of thinking and believe the most talented teams are built by bringing together people of diverse cultures, genders, and backgrounds.

rows.title: AI Engineer – Medical Imaging & Surgical Robotics (Cambridge, MA)
rows.descriptionText:
Job Title

AI Engineer – Medical Imaging & Surgical Robotics (Cambridge, MA)

Job Description

AI Engineer – Medical Imaging & Surgical Robotics (Cambridge, MA)

Join Philips to help shape the next generation of intelligent surgical robotics. In this role, you will work with robotics, software, and clinical experts to develop first-of-a-kind computer vision medical AI solutions that advance autonomy, decision-making, and workflow intelligence for image-guided procedures.

Your Role

Develop and apply AI and computer vision algorithms for medical imaging and image-guided surgical robotics applications.Design, train, evaluate, and optimize deep learning models, including convolutional neural networks, vision transformers, and other modern vision architectures for medical image understanding.Develop methods for object detection, segmentation, registration, image interpretation, tracking, and quantitative image analysis across medical imaging data.Work with imaging modalities relevant to image-guided therapies, such as X-ray, fluoroscopy, DSA, CT, CTA, CBCT, and related 2D/3D imaging sources.Contribute to multimodal sensing and image-based localization methods that support robotic perception, device awareness, and navigation workflows.Develop algorithms and software in a medical device environment, with attention to robustness, traceability, verification, and clinical relevance.Contribute to uncertainty estimation, safety monitoring, failure detection, and performance characterization for AI-enabled imaging and robotic systems.Partner closely with system engineering, robotics, software, clinical, regulatory, and product teams to translate algorithmic concepts into practical, production-oriented solutions.

You're The Right Fit If

You have a Master’s degree with 2+ years of experience OR a PhD in Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field.Your skills include:You have strong experience in computer vision, medical image analysis, or machine learning applied to imaging data.You have hands-on experience developing deep learning models using modern AI/ML frameworks, with practical knowledge of model training, evaluation, validation, and deployment.You have experience with medical image processing techniques such as segmentation, registration, detection, tracking, feature extraction, or 2D/3D image analysis.You are familiar with medical imaging modalities used in image-guided therapies, especially X-ray, CT, CTA, CBCT, 3D rotational angiography, or DSA. Prior experience with these modalities is highly preferred.You have strong programming skills in Python. Experience with C++, software engineering best practices, CI/CD, and production-quality code is preferred.You have experience, or strong interest, in uncertainty estimation, safety-bounded AI, runtime monitoring, robustness testing, or fail-safe behavior for AI-enabled systems.You are comfortable working in a regulated medical device environment and can contribute to technical documentation, validation evidence, and cross-functional design discussions.Publications or research experience in medical image computing, computer vision, or related venues such as MICCAI, IEEE TMI, CVPR, or similar are a plus.You must be able to successfully perform the following minimum Physical, Cognitive and Environmental job requirements with or without accommodation for this position.You possess excellent written and verbal communication skills and are self-motivated with good organizational and time management skills as well as a strong desire to learn and adapt to new technologies and challenges.
How We Work Together

We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

This is an office role.

About Philips

We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help improve the lives of others.

Learn more about our business.Discover our rich and exciting history.Learn more about our purpose.Learn more about our culture.

Philips Transparency Details 

The pay range for this position in Cambridge, MA is $129,000 to $205,000.

The actual base pay offered may vary within the posted ranges depending on multiple factors including job-related knowledge/skills, experience, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

In addition, other compensation, such as an annual incentive bonus, sales commission or long-term incentives may be offered. Employees are eligible to participate in our comprehensive Philips Total Rewards benefits program, which includes a generous PTO, 401k (up to 7% match), HSA (with company contribution), stock purchase plan, education reimbursement and much more. Details about our benefits can be found here.

At Philips, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top end of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each case.

Additional Information

US work authorization is a precondition of employment. The company will not consider candidates who require sponsorship for a work-authorized visa, now or in the future.

Company relocation benefits will not be provided for this position. For this position, you must reside in or within commuting distance to Cambridge, MA.

This requisition is expected to stay active for 45 days but may close earlier if a successful candidate is selected or business necessity dictates. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible to ensure consideration.

Philips is an Equal Employment and Opportunity Employer including Disability/Vets and maintains a drug-free workplace.

rows.title: Business Analyst (New Grad)
rows.descriptionText:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Business Analyst team shapes the strategy, growth, and performance of Robinhood's credit products, delivering top-tier experiences for our users. As part of the broader Credit organization, we work closely with product, engineering, risk, and operations to unlock sustainable business growth through deep analytical rigor. Our team fosters a collaborative, ownership-driven culture where every analyst directly influences business strategy and product direction.

As a Business Analyst, you'll be part of an 18-month rotational program, completing approximately five rotations across different areas of our Money and Growth org. Each rotation embeds you alongside product, engineering, risk, and operations teams — giving you direct exposure to the metrics, stakeholders, and strategic priorities that drive Robinhood's core business. You'll own real work from day one, build cross-functional fluency fast, and leave each rotation having made a measurable impact.

This role is based in our Washington, D.C. office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What You’ll Do

Build fluency across the Money and Growth org by rotating through roughly 5 distinct team assignments over the program, each with its own stakeholders, metrics, and strategic prioritiesAnalyze business performance metrics and economic drivers to identify growth opportunities and optimize business outcomesStructure and solve complex, ambiguous problems across product strategy, pricing, user segmentation, and risk-return trade-offsPartner with engineering, product, risk, and finance teams to execute key strategic initiatives and monitor program efficacyDevelop analytical models, dashboards, and executive-level presentations to inform leadership decision-making and influence core business direction

What You Bring

Experience in business analysis, strategy, management consulting, financial services, or a quantitative analytical roleStrong proficiency in SQL and advanced quantitative modeling techniquesAbility to synthesize complex quantitative findings into clear, actionable recommendations for cross-functional partnersFluency with AI tools, with a genuine interest in staying current as the tools evolveBachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Engineering, Data Science, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience

What We Offer

Challenging, high-impact work to grow your careerPerformance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matchingTop Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependentsAccess to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and moreEmployer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefitsTime off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces

In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits.

Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process.

Base Pay Range

Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC)

$110,000—$110,000 USD

Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity.

If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application.

Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.

rows.title: Network Engineer - TS/SCI Cleared
rows.descriptionText:
Zachary Piper Solutions is seeking an Network Engineer to join a Federal Program located in Newington, VA. The Network Engineer will design, secure, and maintain resilient network architectures that enable uninterrupted communication, real-time data sharing, and mission-critical system availability for government customers in dynamic, high-stakes environments.

Responsibilities of the Network Engineer:

Design, secure, and maintain resilient network architectures that enable uninterrupted communication, real-time data sharing, and mission-critical system availability for government customers in dynamic, high-stakes environmentsArchitect and optimize complex LAN, WAN, data center, and cloud networking solutions to ensure scalability, performance, resiliency, and operational continuity.Lead the engineering, deployment, and lifecycle management of routing and switching technologies, including BGP, OSPF, EIGRP, and advanced Cisco networking platforms.Configure, manage, and troubleshoot Cisco Catalyst, Nexus, and ACI environments while ensuring adherence to organizational standards and best practices.Develop and implement network security solutions including firewalls, VPNs, segmentation, access controls, and Zero Trust architectures to protect sensitive information and critical systems.Monitor network health, performance, capacity, and availability using enterprise tools such as SolarWinds, NetFlow, and Wireshark; identify and resolve issues before they impact mission operations.

Qualifications of the Network Engineer:

Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience)10+ years of related network engineering experience.Active TS/SCI Security ClearanceExpertise in routing and switching protocols such as BGP, OSPF, and EIGRP.Experience with LAN/WAN architecture, design, and deployment.Proficiency with network monitoring and performance tools (e.g., SolarWinds, NetFlow, Wireshark).Hands-on experience with firewalls, VPNs, QoS, and load balancers.Strong background working with Cisco platforms including Catalyst, Nexus, and ACI.

Preferred Qualifications of the Network Engineer:

Experience with SDN and Cisco solutions such as Catalyst Center, ISE, and Intersight.Cloud networking experience (AWS, Azure, GCP).Network automation using Python, REST APIs, Ansible, and Terraform.Knowledge of Zero Trust principles and network security best practices.Familiarity with data center technologies including VXLAN, EVPN, and ACI.

Compensation for the Network Engineer:

Salary Range: $160,000+ *flexible based on experience*Comprehensive Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, PTO, and Sick Leave as required by lawFlexible working scheduleUnlimited opportunities for growth

Key words: networking, network, engineer, engineering, federal, cleared, government, defense, army, lan, wan, design, solarwinds, netflow, wireshark, vpn, qos, load balancers, cisco, nexus, catalyst, aci, bgp, ospf, eigrp, aws, azure, gcp, google cloud, python, ansible, apis, terraform, aero trust, vxlan

rows.title: Software Engineer -  Marketing Systems & Integrations
rows.descriptionText:
Description

Who is USP?

The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide.

At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health.

USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment.

Brief Job Overview

The Software Engineer – Marketo is responsible for supporting and enhancing the Marketo platform through technical configuration, integration management, campaign automation, and data governance. This role partners with IT, Marketing Operations, and Sales Operations to ensure scalable, reliable, and compliant marketing automation processes. The engineer owns day‑to‑day platform operations while contributing to system improvements and cross‑system alignment.

How will YOU create impact here at USP?

As part of our mission to advance scientific rigor and public health standards, you will play a vital role in increasing global access to high-quality medicines through public standards and related programs. USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards.

Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments.

The Software Engineer - Marketing Systems & Integrations has the following responsibilities:

Support user account creation, access permissions, and role governance across marketing automation and CRM platforms to maintain secure, compliant operations.Translate stakeholder requirements into technical configurations, reusable templates, and scalable operational solutions within a marketing automation platform (e.g., Marketo, HubSpot, Pardot, or similar).Help maintain platform architecture — folder structures, naming conventions, tokens, and operational program frameworks.Build and maintain field mappings and synchronization logic between the marketing platform and CRM (e.g., Salesforce), supporting schema alignment and data quality.Clone, configure, and test forms, landing pages, and web assets in Sandbox and Production environments using HTML/CSS fundamentals.Troubleshoot sync issues between systems, including field conflicts, validation errors, and API-related failures — with support from senior engineers as needed.Assist with datatype changes, schema updates, and cross-system compatibility checks to keep integrations stable.Support Sandbox refresh activities: configuration audits, asset restoration, and sync re-establishment.Help build and maintain trigger-based campaigns, automated workflows, and nurture programs, learning platform-specific logic on the job.Assist with segmentation setup, audience management, and basic data governance practices.Monitor system health and campaign performance dashboards, flagging issues to senior team members.Support data quality and compliance standards across marketing and CRM systems.


Who is USP Looking For?

The Successful Candidate Will Have a Demonstrated Understanding Of Our Mission, Commitment To Excellence Through Inclusive And Equitable Behaviors And Practices, Ability To Quickly Build Credibility With Stakeholders, Along With The Following Competencies And Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience).1–2 years of experience in a technical, engineering, or systems support roleWorking knowledge of HTML and CSS; exposure to basic JavaScript is a plus.Understanding of how APIs and webhooks work, or strong aptitude to learn integration concepts quickly.Interest in or exposure to CRM systems (Salesforce, HubSpot, etc.) and/or marketing automation platforms — prior hands-on Marketo experience is not required .Comfort working with structured data: field mapping, data types, and schema logic.Strong problem-solving instincts and willingness to troubleshoot systematically.Clear communicator, able to explain technical issues to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.


Additional Desired (Nice To Have, Not Required)

Any exposure to Marketo, HubSpot, Pardot, or similar marketing automation tools.Familiarity with CRM objects (Leads/Contacts/Accounts/Opportunities).Coursework or personal projects involving REST APIs or third-party integrations (e.g., ad platforms like Google, Meta, or LinkedIn).Certifications are a plus but not expected at this level (e.g., Marketo Certified Associate/Expert, Salesforce Admin).


Supervisory Responsibilities

None, this is an individual contributor role.

Benefits

USP provides the benefits to protect yourself and your family today and tomorrow. From company-paid time off and comprehensive healthcare options to retirement savings, you can have peace of mind that your personal and financial well-being is protected.

Compensation

Base Salary Range: USD $89,816 – $113,450.00 annually.

Target Annual Bonus: % Varies based on level of role.

Individual compensation packages are based on various factors unique to each candidate’s skill set, experience, qualifications, equity, and other job-related reasons.

Note: USP does not accept unsolicited resumes from 3rd party recruitment agencies and is not responsible for fees from recruiters or other agencies except under specific written agreement with USP.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities

This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws.

For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

Job Category Information Technology

Job Type Full-Time

rows.descriptionText:
Piper Companies is seeking a Consultant to support a mission-critical Department of Defense customer in the Washington, DC / Northern Virginia area. This role will focus on the design, development, integration, and enhancement of Appian applications that support secure federal workflows and operational requirements. The ideal candidate will have hands-on Appian development experience, strong application integration skills, and the ability to collaborate with both technical teams and government stakeholders in a secure federal environment.

Responsibilities for the Consultant include:

Design, develop, test, and maintain Appian applications, workflows, and business process solutions using record types, interfaces, process models, business rules, and related platform components.Translate customer requirements into functional Appian applications, user stories, and technical solutions that support mission and business objectives.Build, maintain, and troubleshoot integrations between Appian and enterprise systems using REST APIs, SOAP, JDBC, databases, and other integration technologies.Collaborate with developers, architects, project teams, and government stakeholders throughout the software development lifecycle.Participate in Agile/Scrum activities including sprint planning, backlog refinement, testing, demonstrations, and deployments.Support ongoing application enhancements, maintenance, and issue resolution while ensuring compliance with federal security requirements.

Qualifications for the Consultant include:

Professional experience in software development, application development, technical consulting, or a related technical discipline.Hands-on experience developing Appian applications, including record types, interfaces, process models, business rules, and related application components.Experience integrating Appian with APIs, databases, enterprise systems, and external applications.Experience with REST APIs, SOAP, JDBC, SQL, and relational databases.Understanding of software development principles and experience working in Agile/Scrum environments.Strong analytical, troubleshooting, communication, and problem-solving skills.Active Secret clearance or higher preferred; experience supporting DoD or federal customers, Appian certifications, Appian Data Fabric, AWS, and Security+, CISSP, or related certifications are a plus.

rows.title: Senior Analyst, Revenue and Commissions Operations
rows.descriptionText:
The Revenue and Commissions Team within Finance Operations at Capital One Travel is seeking a Senior Analyst with robust leadership, analytical, and communication abilities. This role requires a professional with exceptional attention to detail and strong problem-solving skills to manage and execute the receivables processes across various functions of the organization. The successful candidate will be instrumental in mitigating operational risks, developing and updating procedural frameworks, and overseeing the reporting of critical payment health metrics. Furthermore, the Senior Analyst will collaborate with diverse teams across Capital One Travel Operations to drive the evolution of receivables workflows toward a future-state model.

Responsibilities:

Accurately collect and reconcile customer receivables. Record and apply customer payments on a daily basis. Follow up with customers on outstanding receivables. Own financial reconciliation data and reporting. Reconcile daily deposits between bank account and accounting system. Monitor inboxes and reply to internal and external stakeholders regarding invoices and payments made to Capital One Travel. Manage and resolve payments in the A/R Suspense account. Manage risks of incorrect receivables by ensuring enhanced controls meet updated payment standards. Partners with Finance, Operations, Product, and Business to streamline processes and resolve payment issues. Reduce operational exceptions and drive efficiencies through automation, elimination, and transfer of manual processes. Understand and own our financial reconciliation data and reporting processesProduce comprehensive and real-time risk reporting and monitoring, including payment health metricsManage risks of incorrect receivables by ensuring team processes are governed by enhanced controls that meet updated payment standardsSupport risk management activities over enhanced control environment, including procedures maintenance, control testing, and process-level assessmentsPartner with Finance, Operations, Product, and Business teams to streamline processes and resolve issues impacting customer receiptsAssist with ad-hoc projects as necessary, such as developing and leading new Finance-

Description 

Project: Large-Scale Logistics System Modernization

 Job Summary 

We are seeking an experienced Oracle Functional Specialist to support the modernization of a major logistics enterprise. The specialist will be a key member of a transformation and integration team, responsible for ensuring the successful implementation and adoption of a new Oracle SaaS-based logistics management system. This role focuses on aligning the system's out-of-the-box (OOTB) capabilities with business requirements, driving process re-engineering, and ensuring the solution meets the strategic objectives of the program. Oracle EBS and Oracle Fusion experience required.

 Key Responsibilities 

Business Process Analysis and Re-engineering:Analyze and document current ("As-Is") logistics and supply chain business processes within legacy systems.Conduct fit-gap analysis to compare business needs against the native capabilities of the Oracle SaaS solution, identifying areas for process improvement and minimizing technical customization.Design and develop optimized ("To-Be") business process maps and workflows that align with industry best practices and leverage standard Oracle SaaS functionality.Business Requirements Management:Collaborate with stakeholders to translate business needs into clear, concise, and comprehensive functional requirements.Manage and govern the requirements lifecycle, ensuring all requirements are captured, tracked, and traced within a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM).Review inbound functional requirements and recommend changes to underlying business processes and/or policies to enable use of Oracle Fusion OOTB capabilities, challenging requests for customization and guiding stakeholders toward standard solutions.System and Solution Analysis:Act as a subject matter expert on the Oracle SaaS solution's logistics and supply chain modules.Provide functional support for testing activities, including facilitating User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to validate that the solution meets business intent and complies with all relevant policies and requirements.Analyze and de-conflict organizational policies, directives, and procedures that may hinder the adoption of modern, industry-standard logistics processes.Data and Compliance:Support the implementation of a data governance and management plan to ensure the integrity, accuracy, and completeness of accountable property data within the new system.Assist in documenting and mapping key security, compliance, and auditability requirements to the system design.

rows.title: ITAM Analyst (SAM/HAM)
rows.descriptionText:
Ideal Candidate Profile: Seeking an ITAM Analyst (SAM/HAM) with Flexara, Software & hardware asset management experience who supports Software Asset Management modernization by managing and improving software contract, entitlement, renewal, usage, ownership, compliance, and vendor data. This role supports software cost optimization, tool rationalization, governed intake, renewal readiness, audit preparation, vendor governance, SAM reporting, and CMDB alignment. The Analyst III helps ensure software assets are visible, governed, cost-effective, compliant, and aligned to enterprise technology standards. This role partners with ITAM, Procurement, Finance, Security, Legal, Workforce, Endpoint, Support Center, Product, application owners, and vendors to improve software lifecycle governance, reduce unmanaged renewals, support self-service software access, strengthen CMDB alignment, and improve leadership visibility through reliable reporting. The Analyst III is expected to analyze software data, identify trends and risks, recommend improvements, coordinate with stakeholders, support complex renewals and software reviews, and help improve SAM processes and controls. The role also requires curiosity and a commitment to keeping up with evolving technology, including SAM platforms, SaaS management tools, Flexera capabilities, automation, AI-enabled productivity tools, software metering, entitlement normalization, CMDB integration, and software governance best practices. In addition to its primary SAM focus, this role provides Hardware Asset Management (HAM) support at the Reston, VA office, including hardware moves, shipping/receiving coordination, inventory reviews, device recovery efforts, and related physical asset activities.

About The Opportunity

The ITAM Analyst Software Asset Management leads operational and analytical work across Client's software asset lifecycle. This role helps govern software inventory, license assignments, entitlements, renewals, usage, application ownership, contract records, vendor performance, compliance evidence, software intake, and lifecycle reporting. The analyst will help advance Software Asset Management modernization by improving data quality, entitlement accuracy, renewal tracking, license visibility, software utilization, compliance readiness, financial transparency, and operational consistency across the software lifecycle. This includes software intake, approval, procurement support, assignment, provisioning coordination, renewal, reclamation, retirement, compliance review, and vendor governance. This role partners closely with ITAM, Procurement, Finance, Security, Legal, Workforce, Endpoint, Support Center, Product, application owners, vendor partners, and other cross-functional teams to reduce software waste, improve service delivery, strengthen compliance, support reliable workforce operations, and provide leadership with trusted reporting. This position requires strong analytical thinking, communication, customer service, attention to detail, follow-through, cross-functional coordination, and the ability to work through complex software issues across multiple systems, teams, vendors, and governance processes. The ITAM Analyst III is expected to apply technology learning in practical ways by leading improvements that reduce manual work, improve software data accuracy, strengthen audit readiness, improve reporting, increase license reuse and reclamation, and enhance the employee software request and fulfillment experience. This role also supports HAM operations at the Reston, VA office, helping ensure hardware moves, shipping/receiving, inventory reviews, and device recovery activities run smoothly.

 Technology and Continuous Learning

The ITAM Analyst III Software Asset Management is expected to stay current with evolving workplace technology, software asset management practices, automation opportunities, and industry trends. This includes developing and applying knowledge of modern SAM platforms, SaaS management tools, license optimization methods, CMDB data practices, software discovery, software metering, AI-enabled productivity tools, reporting dashboards, vendor management capabilities, and compliance practices. The Analyst III should bring a learner's mindset and look for practical ways to apply new tools and technology improvements to reduce manual work, improve data accuracy, strengthen audit readiness, improve software utilization, and enhance the employee software request and fulfillment experience.

 Operational Requirement

Ability to support technology inventory reviews, software true-up activities, audit evidence preparation, vendor data validation, renewal reviews, software utilization analysis, and special projects.

Ability to support hardware-related activities where software entitlement, device assignment, or endpoint software deployment data is required.

Ability to participate in onsite meetings, vendor reviews, audits, operational activities, or cross-functional working sessions as needed.

Ability to manage multiple workstreams, prioritize effectively, and escalate risks or blockers before they impact delivery.

 Physical / Operational Requirement HAM Support

Ability to lift, carry, and move technology equipment weighing up to 50 lbs to support shipping and receiving of hardware.

Ability to support hardware moves, refresh activities, shipping and receiving coordination, inventory reviews, audits, device recovery efforts, and special projects.

Ability to provide off-hours support as needed for hardware moves, refreshes, audits, urgent asset activities, recovery escalations, or special projects.

Ability to participate in onsite meetings, vendor reviews, audits, and operational activities at the Reston, VA office as needed.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

Manage and improve software asset management activities across the full software lifecycle, including intake, request, approval, procurement support, assignment, entitlement tracking, renewal, reclamation, retirement, and compliance review.

Maintain accurate software asset records, including licenses, entitlements, subscriptions, renewals, service agreements, contracts, warranties, vendor contacts, application owners, ownership fields, usage data, and lifecycle information.

Track and update software ownership, usage, assignment, entitlement, renewal status, contract terms, license type, and compliance status to improve visibility and governance.

Analyze software asset data to identify unused licenses, duplicate applications, renewal risks, data gaps, compliance issues, shadow IT indicators, and cost optimization opportunities.

Support software request and fulfillment processes by validating entitlement availability, approval status, licensing requirements, ownership, compliance restrictions, and provisioning readiness.

Perform software license reconciliation, usage review, exception reporting, audit evidence gathering, and SLA Health Check activities.

Generate and distribute software reports, compliance reports, renewal reports, usage reports, lifecycle status reports, vendor performance reports, and trend analyses to support decision-making across ITAM and Technology teams.

Identify software eligible for reclamation, reuse, renewal adjustment, retirement, consolidation, rationalization, or cost optimization.

Support vendor governance activities, including software catalog updates, renewal tracking, SLA review, billing accuracy reviews, contract validation, vendor performance reporting, and service performance reporting.

Collaborate with ITAM, Procurement, Finance, Security, Legal, Workforce, Endpoint, Support Center, Product, application owners, and vendor teams to resolve software asset issues and improve lifecycle processes.

Maintain and improve processes related to software asset management, software compliance, CMDB alignment, vendor governance, software intake, and audit readiness.

Identify process gaps and recommend improvements that reduce manual work, improve software data quality, increase automation, and strengthen license governance.

Support high-risk vendor and software title reviews by validating licensing compliance, renewal readiness, ownership, usage, security review status, and shadow IT exposure.

Keep up with emerging technology, SAM best practices, automation tools, AI-enabled solutions, SaaS management trends, CMDB practices, and software governance capabilities.

Contribute to knowledge base articles, process documentation, standard operating procedures, software request guides, reporting guides, and training materials.

Provide high-quality internal customer support when responding to software-related requests, incidents, escalations, and inquiries.

Provide support for software renewals, audits, true-ups, reclamation efforts, vendor reviews, reporting requests, and special projects as required.

Maintain and govern accurate hardware asset records for laptops, mobile devices, peripherals, and monitors - including warranties, service agreements, assignment details, ownership, location, and lifecycle status.

Support hardware moves, refresh activities, shipping and receiving coordination, inventory reviews, audits, device recovery efforts, and special projects at the Reston, VA office.

Provide off-hours support as needed for hardware moves, refreshes, audits, urgent asset activities, recovery escalations, or special projects.

 Software Asset Lifecycle Operations and Data Accuracy 30%

Maintain accurate software asset records across the full lifecycle, including intake, procurement support, approval, assignment, renewal, reclamation, retirement, and compliance review.

Track software ownership, application owner, vendor, license type, entitlement, subscription term, renewal date, usage status, contract status, and related software asset information.

Perform software asset reconciliation and resolve data discrepancies across systems, reports, tickets, vendor records, procurement files, contract records, CMDB records, and usage dashboards.

Analyze software asset data to identify trends, risks, gaps, unused licenses, duplicate tools, upcoming renewals, compliance issues, and opportunities for optimization.

Support software lifecycle stages, including request, approval, procurement support, provisioning coordination, license assignment, renewal, reclamation, retirement, and exception handling.

Execute and improve processes related to software asset management, software catalog accuracy, license compliance, renewal readiness, and lifecycle governance.

Support end users, managers, application owners, and support teams with software asset-related inquiries, ticket updates, entitlement questions, and escalation support.

Support special software programs, renewal activities, true-ups, audits, reclamation campaigns, application rationalization efforts, and other business priorities as needed.

 Software Licensing, Renewals, Compliance, and Optimization 30%

Track software licenses, subscriptions, entitlements, renewals, service agreements, contracts, maintenance terms, and vendor obligations.

Perform software license reconciliation, normalization, usage analysis, entitlement validation, and compliance review activities.

Monitor upcoming renewals and partner with Procurement, Finance, Legal, Security, application owners, and vendors to support timely renewal decisions.

Identify underused, unused, duplicate, expired, over-provisioned, or non-compliant software assets and recommend corrective actions.

Support software reclamation efforts by identifying inactive users, validating license usage, coordinating removal or reassignment, and updating software records.

Support software request processes by confirming license availability, approval requirements, compliance restrictions, and assignment status.

Help maintain a software catalog that supports clear request paths, approved applications, ownership, licensing requirements, and renewal visibility.

Contribute to cost optimization by improving software utilization, reducing unnecessary renewals, and supporting consolidation or retirement of redundant applications.

 Audit, Compliance, Reporting, Vendor Governance, and CMDB Alignment 25%

Support software audit readiness through evidence gathering, license reconciliation, exception tracking, control validation, and reporting.

Perform SLA Health Checks and remediation follow-up for software asset control gaps, entitlement discrepancies, renewal risks, and compliance exceptions.

Generate recurring reports on software inventory, license utilization, renewal status, entitlement accuracy, vendor performance, billing accuracy, compliance status, and software exceptions.

Support vendor governance activities, including software catalog maintenance, contract review, renewal support, invoice validation, billing accuracy review, and vendor performance reporting.

Help ensure software asset data supports financial stewardship, risk management, audit readiness, vendor accountability, lifecycle planning, and operational decision-making.

Support CMDB alignment by improving data quality across employee, software entitlement, application ownership, vendor, lifecycle, contract, and access-relevant software records.

Monitor software asset trends to identify risks related to unmanaged applications, shadow IT, unused licenses, upcoming renewals, non-compliant software, and data quality gaps.

Partner with ITAM leadership and cross-functional teams to improve software governance, reporting accuracy, compliance confidence, and renewal planning.

 Process Improvement, Automation, Technology Learning, and Team Collaboration 15%

Provide meaningful contributions to team discussions related to software process improvement, operational strategy, technology adoption, asset governance, and future-state SAM modernization.

Identify opportunities to streamline software requests, approval, renewal, reclamation, reporting, compliance, and vendor governance workflows.

Support improvements to Jira, ITSM platforms, CMDB, reporting dashboards, software discovery tools, SaaS management tools, vendor reports, and future Software Asset Management platform capabilities.

Stay current with software asset management best practices, automation, AI-enabled tools, SaaS management trends, license optimization practices, CMDB practices, and emerging workplace technology.

Contribute ideas, documentation, standard operating procedures, knowledge articles, and peer support that advance continuous improvement across SAM operations.

Communicate effectively, build strong relationships, and help resolve software asset issues collaboratively across ITAM, Procurement, Finance, Security, Legal, Workforce, Endpoint, Support Center, Product, application owners, and vendor teams.

Support cross-training peers and resolving software asset issues when first presented without escalation where possible.

Support a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, customer service, and operational excellence across Software Asset Management.

 Hardware Asset Management (HAM) Support Onsite Reston, VA

The following HAM support tasks are performed at the Reston, VA office alongside this role's core SAM responsibilities above. They do not carry a separate percentage allocation against the SAM responsibility totals (which remain 100% as defined); rather, this is supplemental scope tied to the role's onsite HAM presence.

Maintain and govern accurate hardware asset records for laptops, mobile devices, peripherals, and monitors, including warranties, service agreements, assignment details, ownership, location, and lifecycle status.

Support hardware moves, refresh activities, shipping and receiving coordination, inventory reviews, audits, device recovery efforts, and special projects.

Provide off-hours support as needed for hardware moves, refreshes, audits, urgent asset activities, recovery escalations, or special projects.

Required Skills & Experience

Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent experience, in software asset management, technology operations, internal customer support, procurement, licensing, vendor management, or related fields, along with 5-7+ years of experience supporting software asset management, software licensing, SaaS administration, renewal coordination, entitlement tracking, procurement coordination, vendor coordination, or internal technology support.

Strong experience managing software records across the full asset lifecycle, including request, approval, procurement support, assignment, renewal, reclamation, retirement, and compliance review.

Experience tracking and maintaining accurate records for software licenses, subscriptions, entitlements, renewals, service agreements, contracts, application owners, vendors, users, and compliance status.

Ability to analyze software asset data, identify discrepancies, resolve entitlement gaps, document findings, recommend improvements, and follow through on corrective actions.

Experience supporting software request, renewal, reclamation, and compliance processes, including usage review, license reassignment, inactive user cleanup, and escalation of renewal or compliance risks.

Ability to work collaboratively and tactfully with vendors, suppliers, internal customers, managers, ITAM, Procurement, Finance, Security, Legal, Workforce, Endpoint, Support Center, Product, application owners, and other cross-functional partners.

Strong customer service, written communication, and verbal communication skills, including the ability to update tickets, prepare software asset reports, document processes, and explain license or entitlement information clearly.

Curiosity and enthusiasm for learning emerging software asset management practices, automation tools, AI-enabled solutions, CMDB practices, SaaS management platforms, software discovery tools, and industry best practices.

Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, follow established procedures, escalate risks or blockers appropriately, travel as needed, and contribute to continuous improvement across software asset management operations.

Exposure to, or experience supporting, AI-enabled automation, workflow orchestration, or agentic tools within operational or software asset management processes including understanding the importance of human oversight, data quality, security, privacy, governance, and measurable business outcomes when these solutions are applied.

Summary: Within the Card Credit Risk Management organization, the Domestic loss forecasting team is in charge of understanding and projecting how a changing economic and customer environment will impact future credit losses. You will execute projects designed to understand recent credit performance of our domestic card portfolios and generate insights to share with senior leaders. You will also leverage those insights along with forecasting models to generate a loss forecast to inform business strategy and financial reporting.

As a Senior Business Analyst at Capital One, you will apply your strategic and analytical skills to major company challenges. You will team with world-class professionals to develop and test strategies that ultimately impact the bottom line. And you will do it all in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages you to take on new responsibility, promotes continuous learning, and rewards innovation.

General Responsibilities:

Analysis: Identify business challenges and opportunities for improvement and solve for them using analysis to make strategic or tactical recommendationsProduct: Perform modeling/analytics to assist new product and pricing strategies for various lending productsMarketing: Support direct-to-consumer marketing efforts for select products, and strategic intent for products distributed through the retail channel. Help build targeted insights to inform the design and development of new customer experiences, as well as breakthrough technology and concepts designed to deliver on new go to market strategiesCredit Risk: Support step-change improvements in credit performance by connecting drivers of future consumer credit trends to historical behavior, creating risk models, and testing hypotheses using rigorous monitoring and analysisExecution: Involve problem frame-works, develop hypotheses, test and analysis, solution development, scope operational feasibility, lead implementation efforts and develop a monitoring planPartnership: Work closely with colleagues across Capital One including: IT, Sales, Operations, Finance and others to drive improvement in quality, volume, service, and profitabilityStrategic & analytic orientation: A proven track record of decision making and problem solving based on analytics. Conceptual thinking skills must be complemented by a strong quantitative orientation, given that a large part of the business is based on rigorous analytic marketing & credit risk managementStrong business judgment, leadership and integrity: He/she should be a tenacious decision maker, able to bring a healthy, aggressive, yet responsible approach to businessStrong communication skills: Impeccable written and oral communication credentials, coupled with strategic influencing skills and the ability to drive agreement through intellect, interpersonal and negotiation skillsClear results orientation: display an intense focus on achieving both short and long term goals. He/she should be able to drive and execute an agenda in an uncertain and fluid environmentSuccessful track record of thriving in a fast paced, entrepreneurial and dynamic environment. Previous consulting experience is a plus

Basic Qualifications:

At least 2 years of professional experience performing analysisCurrently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Business, Finance, Accounting, Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer engineering, Software engineering, Mechanical engineering, Information Systems or a related quantitative field)A Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Business, Finance, Accounting, Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechanical engineering, Information Systems or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration

rows.descriptionText:
Why Join GEICO?

At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities.

Every day we honor our iconic brand by offering quality coverage to millions of customers and being there when they need us most. We thrive on relentless innovation to exceed our customers' expectations while making a real impact on local communities nationwide.

Founded in 1936, GEICO is a member of the Berkshire Hathaway family of companies and one of the largest auto insurers in the United States. When you join our company, we want you to feel valued, supported, and proud to work here. That's why we offer the GEICO Pledge: Great Company, Great Culture, Great Rewards, and Great Careers.

RAD Business Systems Analyst

Your Impact at GEICO

At GEICO, our Research, Analytics and Development (RAD) team leverages data, technology, analytics, and AI-enabled automation to drive innovation and support strategic business decisions. As a Business Systems Analyst, you will serve in a critical role working closely with business leaders and engineering teams to refine business needs into scalable, data-driven solutions while identifying opportunities to use AI tools to automate business processes, improve reporting, and streamline requirements, testing, and delivery activities.

 

How You’ll Make a Difference

Customer Interaction

Partner with stakeholders and lead cross-functional communication Present updates clearly and build trusted relationships 

Needs Assessment

Gather, document, and refine business and system requirements Translate needs into user stories, workflows, and improvement opportunities Use AI tools to support requirements gathering, documentation, workflow analysis, and automation opportunities across business processes 

Problem Resolution

Analyze issues, test solutions, and identify opportunities to use AI to create test plans, automate test cases, and improve solution validation Support troubleshooting and validate fixes 

Meaningful Impact

Apply AI-enabled automation to improve business processes, data analysis, reporting, and operational efficiency Improve operations through data-driven solutions Promote data standards and Agile progress 

What We’re Looking For  

Experience & Qualifications: 

1–2 years of experience using AI tools to support business process automation, including requirements of documentation, workflow improvements, test planning, test case automation, data analysis, and reporting. Experience eliciting and documenting functional system requirements in partnership with project stakeholders. Experience developing test plans, creating and executing QA or automated test scripts, and validating system functionality through regression and scenario-based testing. 

Core Skills: 

Candidate must possess strong written and verbal communication skills, a demonstrated ability to meet deadlines, a strong analytical ability, and a willingness to respond to ad hoc requests from customers in a timely manner. Must be able to work independently with limited supervision, perform under pressure, and multi-task. 

Preferred Skills: 

Candidate with or pursuing a degree in Information Systems, Computer Science or related field/equivalent experience is preferred. Prior experience in insurance and knowledge on insurance products Agile/SAFE certifications. Experience working in an Agile environment and familiarity with Agile project management practices. Experience with Software Development Life Cycle. Knowledge of Data Management concepts, including data modeling, architecture, and data governance. Working knowledge of SQL is preferred Coding experience and the utilization of AI in code generation for the purpose of creating user interfaces and business support logic. 

Annual Salary

$64,575.00 - $129,150.00

The above annual salary range is a general guideline. Multiple factors are taken into consideration to arrive at the final hourly rate/ annual salary to be offered to the selected candidate. Factors include, but are not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations.

At this time, GEICO will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position.

The GEICO Pledge

Great Company: Protecting customers through life’s twists and turns with innovation and integrity.

Great Careers: Personalized development programs, mentorship, and certification assistance.

Great Culture: Inclusive and collaborative culture rooted in shared success.

Great Rewards: Competitive pay, benefits, and flexibility to support your well-being and future.

GEICO hires and promotes individuals solely on the basis of their qualifications for the job to be filled.

GEICO reasonably accommodates qualified individuals with disabilities to enable them to receive equal employment opportunity and/or perform the essential functions of the job, unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship to the Company.
